The learner asks specifically: Make sure one of the senses is this meaning: to have to have something.

draft.emotion: earnest and direct, asking for help or stating a necessity plainly
notes: Followed directly by a noun ('ho bisogno di aiuto') or an infinitive verb ('ho bisogno di dormire'). When followed by a definite article, 'di' contracts ('ho bisogno del medico').
Also compares with 'servire' ('mi serve un caffè'), which is very common in spoken Italian for needing things.

senses.definition: To require something or someone, or to need to do something.

examples.text: Ho bisogno di un caffè per svegliarmi.
examples.translation: I need a coffee to wake up.
examples.emotion: groggy and hopeful, looking forward to the morning boost

examples.text: Hai bisogno di riposare un po'.
examples.translation: You need to rest a bit.

draftBefore.emotion: earnest and direct, asking for help or stating a necessity plainly
notes: Followed either by a noun (e.g. 'ho bisogno di aiuto') or by 'di' plus an infinitive verb (e.g. 'ho bisogno di dormire').
Do not confuse with the modal verb 'dovere' which expresses obligation rather than an internal necessity or lack.

senses.definition: To require something essential for a purpose or state.

examples.text: Ho bisogno di un caffè per svegliarmi.
examples.translation: I need a coffee to wake up.
examples.emotion: groggy and hopeful, looking forward to the morning boost

senses.definition: To have to have something urgently in order to function or cope.

examples.text: In questo momento ho proprio bisogno di staccare la spina.
examples.translation: Right now I really have to have a break from everything.
examples.emotion: exhausted and stressed, craving some peace and quiet

faults.quote: (dependency) To have to have something urgently in order to function
faults.why: Senses 0 and 1 are the exact same meaning ('to need').
